edges.reason: Language models are a specialized topic within NLP and require basic understanding of language processing tasks and concepts.
Attention mechanisms are typically taught as neural network components and require deep learning foundations.
Modern language models are primarily built using deep learning architectures.
Language models fundamentally model likelihoods of sequences and require understanding probability.
Core NLP methods rely on probabilistic reasoning for modeling uncertainty and language phenomena.
Deep learning training and loss formulations commonly depend on probabilistic concepts.
Attention uses normalized weighting and uncertainty-related concepts that rely on probability foundations.
Training models requires understanding probabilistic objectives, likelihoods, and uncertainty.
Deep learning depends on optimization methods to fit neural network parameters.
Training models requires optimization to minimize loss and improve predictions.
Deep learning requires data to be encoded into numerical representations suitable for neural networks.
Language models require text to be represented as tokens, embeddings, or similar encodings.
Attention operates over structured vector representations of inputs.
Efficient implementation of machine learning algorithms presumes understanding the model training process being executed.
